problems: The blind guess ('standing human with arms spread, front-on') does not match the intended gull. The figure reads as a bird in flight with spread wings, which was only the secondary alternative.
The body is too thin for 'plump'. The breast star (116602) sits on a narrow torso, so the 'centre of the plump body' part is not carried by the silhouette.
Labels collide: 'breast, centre of the plump body' runs into 'right wing shoulder, on the leading edge'. The right wingtip label is clipped at the right edge ('brightest sta').
The tail fork star (117315) sits inside the tail region, but the tail outline is faint and reads as legs or a stray shape rather than a forked tail.

Stars 116231 (beak tip), 116389 (neck), 765 (far-left wingtip), 114421 (right shoulder), 112122 (right wingtip) and 112623 (trailing corner) sit on plausible parts. Gold lines trace a skeleton over a blue outline, so this is not a plain copy of the gold lines.
Several unlabelled white stars sit outside the figure and add visual noise. Their role is unclear.
output.advice: Redraw so the silhouette reads unmistakably as a gull in flight. Keep the head and beak upright at the top (116231 to 116389 neck). Give the body a visibly rounder belly around the breast star (116602), roughly doubling its width. Keep the wings spread with the far-left tip at 765 and the right shoulder at 114421 on the leading edge, and the right wingtip at 112122, which is the brightest star. Make the trailing corner at 112623 the rear wing edge. Make the tail a clear forked fan whose centre is 117315. Move the breast label away from the right-shoulder label, and shorten the wingtip label so it is not clipped. Remove or dim unlabelled stray stars so the key stars carry the figure.
